summary: The note surveys how local schools expanded extracurricular programs from the 2023-2024 academic year to boost student engagement, covering holistic development, arts, sports, STEM, service and entrepreneurship initiatives. It cites specific programs, launch dates and educators, along with a CEI report linking participation to better grades and attendance. It also stresses parent and community support and a continued expansion of offerings.
one_line: Local schools launched varied extracurricular programs in 2023-2024 to boost engagement, with a CEI report linking them to better grades and attendance.
key_facts: Lincoln High School launched the Holistic Development Program (HDP) on September 5, 2023, led by Principal Angela Martinez, in response to concerns about student participation and mental health.
Jefferson Middle School offers robotics and coding clubs, language cafés, and environmental stewardship organizations.
The Diversity in Dialogue forum at Jefferson Middle School began October 15, 2023, created by Rebecca Sun and Jerome K. Thompson to foster discussion of global affairs and multiculturalism.
Riverdale Elementary School introduced "Move-n-Learn" on November 1, 2023, led by phys-ed coach Mike Henderson, combining physical activity with academic goals such as math and science.
At Central High School, drama teacher Catherine Young directed a lauded production of "Our Town"; a theatre night performance took place October 25, 2023.
Harrison Tech dedicates Wednesdays to extracurricular STEM learning under newly appointed STEM coordinator Dr. Lewis Schmidt.
Harrison Tech's robotics team won the regional championship on November 22, 2023.
Summit Preparatory School's Community Outreach and Leadership Lab began September 27, 2023, with projects ranging from food drives to tutoring younger students; Olivia Grant is co-facilitator.

A December 8, 2023 report by the Center for Educational Improvement (CEI) found extracurricular students often show improved grades, better time-management, more self-confidence, and less absenteeism.
Monroe High School established the "Future Entrepreneurs Club" on September 30, 2023, in partnership with the local Chamber of Commerce.
Local businesses sponsor events and volunteers from various industries share expertise with students.
